Background

Hi, I am Joel Varghese. I started my career in digital marketing and business development, running campaigns, building brand strategies, and learning fast what actually moves the needle. That experience, backed by an MBA, gave me a strong foundation in how businesses operate and how audiences think.

Moving to Canada opened a new chapter. I crossed into UX and realized it was the same game I had always been playing, just with sharper tools, a cleaner process, and a deeper focus on the human side of things.

I have worked in agencies, hotels, and fast paced client facing environments across two countries. I am eager to grow, contribute, and be part of something that actually makes an impact.

UX Research and Information Architecture

City of Kingston Grants Portal

A multi phase UX research and design project focused on understanding and improving how the City of Kingston manages its internal grant programs. The project covered the full research lifecycle from secondary research through focus groups, partner interviews, and a final prototype delivered directly to the City of Kingston grants team.

Case Study 01

City of Kingston Grants Portal

Role
UX Researcher and Designer
Client
City of Kingston
Tools
Figma, Miro, Google Forms
Type
Team Research Project

Overview

The City of Kingston manages multiple grant programs across departments using fragmented systems including email submissions, Excel spreadsheets, Dropbox storage, and Google Drive. This project identified critical pain points in the existing process and designed a centralised portal solution to improve efficiency, reduce administrative burden, and enhance coordination between City staff and partner organisations.

The research was carried out across three phases covering secondary research, primary research with City staff, and primary research with partner organisations, resulting in a journey map, prototype, and final recommendations delivered directly to the City of Kingston grants administration team.

Research Process

Three Phase Approach
01

Secondary Research

Scanned six Canadian municipalities and reviewed grant management literature to understand the landscape before engaging City staff directly.

02

Focus Group

Conducted a 60 minute focus group with five City staff members across three departments to map the full grant lifecycle and identify breakdowns.

03

Partner Interviews

Conducted in depth interviews with partner organisations to validate focus group findings with real operational experience from the field.

Key Findings

The research surfaced seven critical findings that directly shaped the design direction.

Partners Handle Core Admin

Partner organisations manage eligibility review, jury coordination, applicant support, and score compilation entirely outside City systems.

Incomplete Applications Waste Time

Reviewing applications for missing documents takes several days to a week every cycle. Signatures are the most common missing item.

Adaptive Forms Needed

Forms should auto adjust based on applicant type. Built in tips for each question would reduce confusion without lengthening submissions.

Jury Process Entirely Manual

Applications distributed via Dropbox, scores collected on paper. Manual spreadsheet compilation before every adjudication meeting.

No Cross Department Visibility

Each department uses different tools. Duplicate applicants discovered informally during jury discussions rather than caught systematically.

Post Award Work Underestimated

Grant agreements, installment tracking, interim reports, and final reports all handled manually with workload chronically underestimated.

Design Recommendations

Centralised Portal

Build a unified portal connecting all programs, tracking, review, and reporting into one shared system for both City staff and partners.

Automated Validation

Portal validates all required documents and signatures before submission, eliminating the manual screening week and reducing follow up.

Adaptive Application Forms

Forms auto populate based on program type and applicant status with built in contextual tips to reduce confusion.

Integrated Jury Management

Jurors access applications on the portal with secure viewing, digital score submission, and automated confidentiality enforcement.

Multi User Access Control

Both City and partner organisations receive administrative permissions so partners can screen applications without waiting for City handoff.

Structured Post Award Workflow

Grant agreements, installment schedules, and report deadlines tracked in system with automated reminders replacing scattered email management.

Key Insights

01

Built on Dedication

At every stage, staff are manually bridging gaps that a well designed system would handle automatically.

02

Applicants Deserve Clarity

A connected system means better communication, less confusion, and more trust between the City and its community.

03

Kingston Is Ready

The foundation is strong, the people are committed, and a unified platform is the natural next step for a city that takes its community seriously.

Outcomes and Reflections

Working directly with the City of Kingston grants team gave this project real stakes. Every research decision had to be grounded and defensible. The focus group and partner interviews revealed a gap between what City leadership assumed and what partner organisations were actually managing on their behalf. Translating that into a concrete design direction taught me how to move from empathy to evidence to recommendation in a way that serves both users and stakeholders.
